Here is a refutation and denunciation of those who deny the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ), even though he came with the same kind of signs that the messengers before him brought, and greater ones than them.

How, then, can his prophethood be denied? It is not one of the matters that are unknown to the world. Indeed, the earth has never been without messengers and their traces. Your Messenger came along the same path as the messengers who preceded him in their mission, and he was not an innovation (bid'an).

(Section)

Al-Suhayli said: When the ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, "state" or "circumstance" of the noun) is a quality that is inseparable from the noun, it is more appropriate to construe it as a descriptive attribute (na't) of that noun.

When it is equivalent to a verb and not inseparable from the noun, except at the time of predicating the verb of it, while it is a ḥāl, because it is derived from "change" (taḥawwul), it can only be a quality from which one changes. For this reason it is only derived from a verb, since the verb is a movement that is not fixed. It may come underived but with the meaning of a derived form, as in his saying:

"And at times the angel appears to me in the form of a man"

narrated by Muslim.

That is: he changes from his state and returns, taking the form of a man. So his saying "rajulan" (a man) carries the sense of "taṣawwuran" (appearing) in this form. As for their saying, "Zayd came to me a righteous man" (jā'anī Zaydun rajulan ṣāliḥan), the attribute has prepared the noun for the ḥāl, and were it not for ṣāliḥan, "rajulan" would not be a ḥāl. Likewise is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿a tongue, Arabic﴾ (lisānan ʿarabiyyan).

I say: On this basis the types of ḥāl are four: restrictive (muqayyida), presumptive (muqaddara), emphatic (mu'akkida), and preparatory (muwaṭṭi'a).

If it is asked: What is the benefit of mentioning the solid noun (ism jāmid) in the preparatory type, and why not suffice with the derived noun in it? It is answered: Mentioning the noun qualified by the attribute in this position is evidence that this ḥāl is binding on its bearer and that it is permanent for him. It is not like your saying "Zayd came to me righteous" (jā'anī Zaydun ṣāliḥan), because "ṣāliḥan" contains only the form of a verb, and the verb is not lasting. But in your saying "rajulan ṣāliḥan" there is the word "rajul," which is lasting, and therefore it was mentioned.

If it is asked: How can "lisānan ʿarabiyyan" be a ḥāl when it is not a transient attribute? This is why, if you said "Zayd came to me a Qurashi" or "an Arab," it would not be permitted.

It is answered: His saying "lisānan ʿarabiyyan" is a ḥāl from the pronoun in "muṣaddiq" (confirming), not from "kitāb" (Book), because the latter is indefinite, and the element governing the ḥāl is the meaning of the verb within "muṣaddiq." So the meaning becomes that it confirms you in this state. The noun that is the bearer of the ḥāl is eternal, and it had not been described by this attribute when its meaning, not its wording, was sent down to Moses, Jesus, and the messengers who preceded them. It became Arabic only when it was sent down to Muhammad ﷺ, confirming what was before it of the Book. So the meaning of the ḥāl has been made clear and the difficulty removed.

I say: No, rather you have increased the difficulty by adding to it, and the meaning of the verse is not what you have claimed. Rather, "lisānan ʿarabiyyan" is a ḥāl from "kitāb," and the ḥāl is valid from it despite its being indefinite, because it has been qualified, and an indefinite noun when qualified may have a ḥāl from it, just as it is valid to begin with it.

As for his saying that the meaning is "confirming you," there is no doubt that it confirms you, but the intended meaning of the verse is that it confirms what came before of the Books of God, Exalted is He, as He said: ﴿And We revealed to you the Book with the truth, confirming what is before it of the Book﴾

And He said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. God, there is no god but Him, the Living, the Self-Subsisting. He has sent down to you the Book with the truth, confirming what is before it﴾

And He said: ﴿And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed, confirming that which is before it﴾

Do you not see how it has been consistent in the Qur'an to describe the Book as confirming what is before it?

He also said: By the consensus of the people, the intended meaning is that it confirms the books that preceded it. By this path it also confirms the Prophet ﷺ, and it is a stronger proof of his truthfulness than saying, "This is a Book confirming you," for when the earlier Books confirm it and bear witness to the soundness of what is in it, revealed by God without collusion or borrowing from them, this shows that what the Messenger of God ﷺ brought is true, just as what they brought is so, and that the source of both is one niche (mishkāt).

For this reason al-Najashi said when the Qur'an was recited to him: "Indeed, this and what Moses brought come out of one niche."

That is: if Moses was truthful and his Book is true, then this too is so, since it is impossible for two things to come out of one niche while one is purely false and the other purely true.

This is only possible with the utmost difference and opposition.

So the Qur'an confirms the earlier Books, and they gave good news of it and of the one who would bring it. The proof of its truth is established from both aspects together: from the good news given of it by those who preceded it, and from its confirming and agreeing with them. So reflect on this.

For this reason this meaning recurs often in the Qur'an, since within it lies an argument against the People of the Book for the truth of [the Prophet] ﷺ by this path. It is also a proof against others by way of necessary implication, for when he brought the like of what they brought without learning a single letter from them, this shows that it is from God, Exalted is He. Even if they denied the messengers who came before, his bringing the like of what they brought would establish his own prophethood and the prophethood of those before him, and be evidence for the soundness of both Books and the truthfulness of both Messengers, because the latter brought a matter that cannot be attained by teaching at all, nor any part of it.

He came with it as an unlettered man who neither reads a book nor writes it with his right hand, nor kept company with any of the People of the Book. Rather, he grew up among you while you witnessed his condition, at home and on journeys, in travel and in residence. This is among the greatest proofs that what he brought is not from human beings and is not within their capacity, and this is a clear proof, as clear as the sun.

What he brought contains the confirmation of those who came before him, and contains the good news of him given by those who preceded him. Thus the proofs and clear signs of God agree on the truthfulness of His prophets and messengers, the excuse is cut off, the argument is established, and nothing remains for the disbeliever except sheer obstinacy, or turning away and obstruction.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 46, verse 15:

He, the Most High, informed that the duration of pregnancy and weaning is thirty months, and in the verse of al-Baqarah He informed that the full period of nursing is two complete years. So it is known that the remainder is suitable as the duration of pregnancy, which is six months. The jurists all agreed that a woman does not give birth in less than six months, unless it is a miscarriage, and this is a matter the jurists received from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Al-Bayhaqi and others narrated from Abu Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad al-Dili that a woman was brought to Umar who had given birth after six months, so Umar intended to stone her. This reached Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said, "There is no stoning upon her." This reached Umar, so he sent for him and asked him, and he said, ﴿And the mothers suckle their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233].

And He said, ﴿And its carrying and its weaning is thirty months﴾.

So six months is the carrying, and two years is the completion of nursing, and there is no punishment upon her. So Umar let her go.

In the Muwatta' of Malik, it reached him that Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, was brought a woman who had given birth after six months, so he ordered that she be stoned. Ali said, "That is not upon her. Allah the Most High said, ﴿And its carrying and its weaning is thirty months﴾

and He said, ﴿And its weaning is in two years﴾." So Uthman ordered that she be returned, and they found that she had already been stoned.

Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he used to say: if a woman gives birth at nine months, the nursing due to her is twenty-one months; if she gives birth at seven months, the nursing due to her is twenty-three months; and if she gives birth at six months, the nursing due to her is twenty-four months, as the Most High said, ﴿And its carrying and its weaning is thirty months﴾. End of his words.

(Benefit)

Ibn Abbas understood that a woman may give birth at six months, but Uthman did not understand this, so he intended to stone a woman who had given birth after six months, until Ibn Abbas reminded him of it, and he acknowledged it.

(Section: The age of ashudd)

When his puberty is certain, the pen of obligation applies to him and all the rulings of a man become established for him; then he begins to reach ashudd (the age of full strength).

Al-Zajjaj said: ashudd is from about seventeen years to about forty.

Ibn Abbas said, in the narration of Ata from him, that ashudd is the age of reaching maturity (al-hulm), and this is the choice of Yahya ibn Ya'mar and al-Suddi.

Mujahid narrated from him: thirty-six years.

He also narrated from him: thirty.

Al-Dahhak said: twenty years.

Muqatil said: eighteen years.

Al-Zuhri has indeed clarified the term, saying: the reaching of ashudd occurs from the time a person attains the status of men until forty years.

He said: the beginning of reaching ashudd is bounded, its end is bounded, and what lies between them is not bounded.

So reaching ashudd is a rank between puberty and forty.

The meaning of the word is from shiddah, which is strength, vigour and forcefulness; a shadid man is a strong man, so ashudd means the strongest.

Al-Farra' said: its singular in analogy is shiddah, but I have not heard a singular for it.

Abu al-Haytham said: its singular is shiddah, like ni'mah and an'um.

Some of the lexicographers said: its singular is shuddah with a dammah on the shin.

Others among them said it is a singular noun like al-aank, and not a plural; Ibn al-Anbari related both opinions.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 46, verse 20:

The most perfect of people are those who guard themselves in this world against what is forbidden. Just as whoever drank wine in this world will not drink it in the Hereafter, whoever wore silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter, and whoever ate from vessels of gold and silver in this world will not eat from them in the Hereafter, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "They are for them in this world, and for you in the Hereafter."

Whoever takes his good things and pleasures in full and uses them up in this abode will be deprived of them there, just as Allah the Exalted condemned those who used up their good things in the worldly life and enjoyed them. For this reason the Companions and those who followed them feared this greatly.

Imam Ahmad mentioned from Jabir ibn Abdullah that Umar saw him carrying meat that he had bought for his family for a dirham. He said: "What is this?"

He said: "Meat I bought for my family for a dirham."

So he said: "Does every one of you buy whatever he craves? Have you not heard Allah the Exalted say: ﴿You used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾?

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said:

The delegation of the people of Basra came with Abu Musa to Umar, and we would enter upon him every day, and his bread was three (kinds). Sometimes we would find it with ghee as a condiment, sometimes we would find it with oil, sometimes we would find it with milk, sometimes we would find dried strips of meat that had been crushed and then heated with it, and sometimes we would find wide pieces of meat, which were few.

One day he said: "By Allah, I see your disgust and your aversion to my food. By Allah, if I wished, I would be among the best of you in food and the most comfortable in living. But I heard the Messenger of Allah say:

He rebuked a people for a matter they had done, and said: ﴿You used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾."

Whoever leaves forbidden pleasure for the sake of Allah will enjoy it on the Day of Resurrection in its most complete form.

Whoever enjoys it here will be deprived of it there, or its perfection will be diminished. Allah does not grant the pleasure of one who debases himself in His disobedience and prohibitions like the pleasure of one who abandons his desire for Allah, ever. And Allah knows best.

(Section)

Some of the early generation said: Among the reward of a good deed is a good deed after it, and among the punishment for a bad deed is a bad deed after it. Among it is his knowledge of the loss of what is more beloved to him and better for him, of the same kind or of a different kind, for Allah does not combine for His servant the pleasure of forbidden things in this world and the pleasure of what is in the Hereafter.

As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire: "You used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 20].

So the believer does not use up his good things in this world; rather he must leave some of his good things for the Hereafter.

As for the disbeliever, he does not believe in the Hereafter, so he is greedy to take all his portions and good things in this world. Among it is his knowledge that his deeds are his provision and his means to his abode. If he provides himself with disobedience to Allah, that provision brings him to the abode of the disobedient and the criminals; and if he provides himself with obedience to Him, he arrives at the abode of the people of His obedience and allegiance. Among it is his knowledge that his deed is his guardian in his grave, his companion in it, his intercessor before his Lord, and the one who disputes and argues on his behalf; if He wills, He makes it for him, and if He wills, He makes it against him. Among it is his knowledge that deeds of righteousness raise the servant up, sustain him, and ascend with him to Allah; so in proportion to the strength of his attachment to them will be his ascent along with their ascent. Deeds of wickedness drag him down, pull him toward the pit, and drag him to the lowest of the low; and in proportion to the strength of his attachment to them will be his descent with them and his fall to where they settle him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿To Him ascend the good word, and the righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10].

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾ [al-A'raf: 40].

So when the gates of heaven were not opened for their deeds but were shut against them, they are not opened for their souls at the time of departure but are shut against them.

As for the people of faith and righteous deeds, when the gates of heaven were open for their deeds until they reached Allah the Exalted, their souls were opened for them until they reached Him, stood before Him, and He showed mercy to them and ordered the writing of their names in 'Illiyyun. Among it is his leaving the fortress of Allah, in which there is no loss for whoever enters it; so by his disobedience he leaves it for a place where he becomes plunder for thieves and highway robbers.

So what is the thought of one who leaves a secure fortress, where no calamity reaches him, for a desolate ruin that is the refuge of thieves and highway robbers? Would they leave with him any of his belongings?

Among it is that by disobedience he exposes himself to the erasure of blessing in everything of his worldly and otherworldly affairs; for obedience brings the servant the blessings of everything, while disobedience erases every blessing from him.

In sum, the effects of ugly disobedience are more than the servant can comprehend, and the effects of good obedience are more than he can comprehend. The good of this world and the Hereafter in its entirety is in obeying Allah, and the evil of this world and the Hereafter in its entirety is in disobeying Him.

And in some narrations Allah the Exalted says: "Who is it that obeyed Me and was made wretched by his obedience to Me? And who is it that disobeyed Me and was made happy by his disobedience to Me?"

Ibn al-Qayyim, Tafsir al-Qayyim, on Surah 46 (al-Ahqaf), verse 26:

Consider His words: ﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you﴾.

See how the meaning is that your ruling is like their ruling: since We destroyed them for disobeying Our messengers, and the things they were empowered with of the means of livelihood did not avert it from them, then you are likewise, an equalizing between two like cases, and that this is the pure justice of Allah among His servants.

(Benefit)

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And [mention] when We turned toward you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. And when they attended it, they said, "Be silent." And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners.﴾ up to His words: ﴿Those are in manifest error.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29-32]

This indicates that the jinn are under obligation (taklif) in several respects:

First: Allah, glorified and exalted, turned them toward His Messenger to listen to the Qur'an, so that they would believe in it, comply with its commands, and refrain from its prohibitions.

Second: They turned back to their people as warners (mundhirin), and warning (al-indhar) is informing of a fear once its causes have been established. It is therefore known that they warned their people of the Fire if they disobeyed the Messenger.

Third: They reported that they had heard the Qur'an, understood it, comprehended it, and that it guides to the truth. This statement of theirs indicates that they know about Moses and the Book revealed to him, and that the Qur'an confirms it and guides to the straight path.

This indicates that they were enabled with knowledge by which the proof is established, and that they are capable of acting upon what it contains; and obligation necessarily entails reason and capability.

Fourth: They said to their people: ﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31]

This is explicit that they are obligated and commanded to respond to the Messenger, which means affirming what he reports and obeying what he commands.

Fifth: They said: ﴿He will forgive you some of your sins﴾. Forgiveness occurs only for a sin, which is opposing a command.

Sixth: They said: ﴿some of your sins﴾, and sin is opposing a command.

Seventh: They said: ﴿and protect you from a painful punishment﴾. This indicates that whoever of them does not respond to the caller of Allah is not protected from the painful punishment. This is explicit in the attachment of the Islamic law (al-shari'ah al-Islamiyyah) to them.

Eighth: They said: ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will not be able to escape on earth, and he will have no protectors besides Him.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32]

This is a threat to whoever among them refuses to respond to the caller of Allah. It has been cited as evidence that they were worshipping under the law of Moses just as they are worshipping under the law of Muhammad. This is possible, but the verse does not necessarily imply it. However, the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-An'am: 130]

This verse indicates that the jinn were worshipping under the laws of the messengers before Muhammad ﷺ, and the preceding verses also indicate this.

Based on this, the Prophet ﷺ's being sent to both groups (al-thaqalayn) means to all of them, not to some of them.

Before him, a messenger would be sent to a particular group. Also, Allah, the Exalted, said about His Prophet Solomon: ﴿And among the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord; and whoever deviates among them from Our command, We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.﴾ [Saba': 12]. This is pure obligation.

[Chapter: On the death of Abu Talib and the death of Khadijah, and the departure to al-Ta'if]

When the document was annulled, the death of Abu Talib and the death of Khadijah coincided, with little time between them. So the affliction upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the foolish among his people intensified, and they became bold against him and openly harmed him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to al-Ta'if, hoping they would shelter him, support him against his people, and protect him from them. He invited them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but he found no one who would give him shelter and no supporter. They harmed him with the greatest harm, and they inflicted upon him what his own people had not inflicted. Zayd ibn Harithah, his freedman, was with him. He remained among them for ten days, not leaving any of their nobles without going to him and speaking to him. They said: "Leave our land," and they incited their foolish ones against him. They lined up on both sides for him and began pelting him with stones until his feet bled, while Zayd ibn Harithah shielded him with his own body until he was struck with wounds on his head. He returned from al-Ta'if to Makkah, grieved. On that return he supplicated with the well-known supplication of al-Ta'if: "O Allah, to You I complain of the weakness of my strength, the scarcity of my resources, and my lowliness before people. O Most Merciful of the merciful, You are the Lord of the weak and You are my Lord. To whom will You entrust me? To a distant one who frowns at me, or to an enemy You have given authority over my affair? If there is no anger from You upon me, I do not mind, though Your well-being is more expansive for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your Face by which the darknesses are illuminated and by which the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set right, that Your wrath descend upon me or Your displeasure befall me. To You is the right of blame until You are pleased, and there is no power nor strength except by You."

Then his Lord, blessed and exalted, sent to him the angel of the mountains, asking his permission to bring the two mountains together upon the people of Makkah, namely the two mountains between which it lies. He said: "No, rather I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins those who worship Him and associate nothing with Him."

When he halted at Nakhlah on his return, he stood to pray during the night, and a group of the jinn was turned toward him, and they listened to his recitation. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not aware of them until there was revealed to him: ﴿And [mention] when We turned toward you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. And when they attended it, they said, "Be silent." And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners — they said, "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path. O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment. And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will not be able to escape on earth, and he will have no protectors besides Him. Those are in manifest error."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29-32].

He remained at Nakhlah for some days. Zayd ibn Harithah said to him: "How will you enter upon them when they have expelled you?" meaning the Quraysh. He said: "O Zayd, Allah will surely make for what you see a relief and a way out, and Allah will surely support His religion and make His Prophet victorious."

Then he arrived at Makkah, and he sent a man from Khuza'ah to Mut'im ibn 'Adi: "May I enter under your protection?" He said: "Yes." He summoned his sons and his people and said: "Put on your weapons and stand at the corners of the House, for I have granted protection to Muhammad." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered, with Zayd ibn Harithah with him, until he reached the Sacred Mosque. Mut'im ibn 'Adi stood upon his mount and called out: "O assembly of Quraysh, I have granted protection to Muhammad, so let none of you harm him." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached the Corner, touched it, prayed two rak'ahs, and returned to his house, while Mut'im ibn 'Adi and his sons surrounded him with weapons until he entered his house.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 46, verse 30:

As for His mention of it [al-sirat, "the path"] with the word "al-tariq" (the way) specifically in Surat al-Ahqaf, this is God the Exalted relating the speech of the believing jinn, that they said to their people: ﴿Indeed, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path.﴾ Their expression here, "al-tariq," contains a wonderful subtle point: they had mentioned Moses before it, and the Book they heard confirmed what was before it of the Book of Moses and others. So it was, in it, like the report about the Messenger of God ﷺ in his saying to his people: ﴿I am not an innovation among the messengers﴾, meaning, I am not the first messenger sent to the people of the earth. Rather, messengers from God had already gone before to the nations, and I was only sent confirming them with the same thing they were sent with, namely monotheism and faith. Thus the believing jinn said: ﴿Indeed, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path.﴾ That is, to a trodden way over which the messengers had passed before him, and that he is not an innovation, as He said at the beginning of the same surah.

Eloquence and inimitability therefore required the word "al-tariq" (the way), because it is on the pattern fa'il in the sense of maf'ul (trodden). That is, a path over which the messengers and prophets walked before.

Thus it is binding upon whoever affirms the messengers of God and believes in them to believe in this (Book) and affirm it. So mentioning "al-tariq" here is more appropriate, because it is more fitting to the domain of calling (to God) and to alerting people to the necessity of following it.

And God knows best.

Then I saw that al-Suhayli had mentioned this very same meaning, and his thought coincided with mine.

(Section: On explaining the varying degrees of patience)

Patience, as mentioned earlier, is of two kinds: chosen (ikhtiyari) and compelled (idtirari).

The chosen kind is more perfect than the compelled kind, for the compelled kind is shared by people in general and may be found in those who are not capable of chosen patience. For this reason, the patience of Yusuf the Just, peace be upon him, in refusing the seduction of the wife of the chief minister, and his patience over what he endured in that matter of imprisonment and hardship, was greater than his patience over what he endured from his brothers when they threw him into the well, separated him from his father, and sold him as a slave. Of the second kind is what God, glorified is He, brought about for him: the honor, elevation, kingship, and establishment in the land that He granted him.

Likewise was the patience of the Friend (al-Khalil, Ibrahim), peace be upon him, and of the Interlocutor (al-Kalim, Musa), and the patience of Nuh, and the patience of al-Masih (Isa), and the patience of the Seal of the Prophets and the master of the descendants of Adam, may prayers and peace be upon them all. Their patience was patience in calling to God and in striving against the enemies of God. For this reason God named them Ulu al-Azm (the possessors of resolve), and commanded His Messenger to be patient with the patience they showed, saying: ﴿So be patient as the possessors of resolve among the messengers were patient﴾.

The Ulu al-Azm are those mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He has prescribed for you of religion what He enjoined upon Nuh, and that which We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa﴾.

And in His saying: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa﴾.

Likewise said Ibn Abbas and others from among the early generations (al-salaf).

[Benefit: A writing for difficult childbirth]

Al-Khallal said: Abdullah ibn Ahmad told me, saying: I saw my father write for a woman when her delivery was difficult, in a white bowl or some clean vessel, writing the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him: "There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds." And: ﴿As if on the day they see what they are promised, they will not have remained but an hour of a day. [It is] a notification﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35], and ﴿As if on the day they see it, they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46].

Al-Khallal said: Abu Bakr al-Marwazi informed us that a man came to Abu Abdullah and said: "O Abu Abdullah! Will you write for a woman whose child has been difficult for her for two days?" He said: "Tell him: let him bring a wide bowl and saffron." And I saw him write for more than one person. He related from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said:

"Isa, may God's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet and upon him, passed by a cow whose calf had become lodged in its belly. It said: 'O Word of God! Pray to God that He release me from what I am in.' He said: 'O Creator of the soul from the soul, O Deliverer of the soul from the soul, O Bringer-forth of the soul from the soul, release it.'

He said: So she cast her calf, and behold, she was standing sniffing it."

He said: If a woman's child is difficult for her, write it for her. And whatever preceded of incantations (ruqa), its writing is beneficial.

A group of the early generations permitted writing some of the Qur'an and drinking it, considering that to be among the healing that God placed in it.

Another writing for this purpose: it is written in a clean vessel: ﴿When the sky is split open, and it responds to its Lord and it is obligated to; and when the earth is stretched out, and throws out what is within it and empties itself﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 1-4].

The pregnant woman drinks from it, and it is sprinkled on her belly.
